draft.title: The greenhouse effect
card: Earth's surface is warmed by sunlight. It gives off heat, which travels back up through the atmosphere towards space.
Greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour, absorb some of this heat. They send some of it back towards the surface, so less heat escapes to space.
This natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life. Without it, Earth's average temperature would be far below freezing.
When there is more of these gases in the atmosphere, more heat is trapped. This makes Earth's average temperature rise.
draft.remember: Greenhouse gases slow heat loss to space, so more gas means more trapped heat.

a.q: What do greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide do in the atmosphere?
opts: Absorb some heat leaving Earth and send some back
Block sunlight so that it never reaches Earth's surface
Make heat that warms the atmosphere from within it
Reflect all heat from the surface straight into space
a.why: Greenhouse gases absorb some of the heat given off by Earth's surface and send some back down, so less escapes to space. They do not stop sunlight reaching the surface, which is what warms it in the first place.
a.clue: Think about heat leaving Earth, not sunlight arriving.

b.q: Planet X and Planet Y receive the same sunlight. Planet X has an atmosphere with more greenhouse gases than Planet Y. What is most likely?
opts: Planet X traps more heat and is warmer on average
Planet X traps less heat and is cooler on average
Planet X has the same temperature as Planet Y
Planet X gets more sunlight, so it is warmer on average
b.why: More greenhouse gases absorb and return more of the heat leaving the surface, so less escapes and the planet is warmer. The sunlight is the same, so the difference comes from the atmosphere, not from the amount of sunlight received.
b.clue: The sunlight is equal, so look at what happens to the heat leaving.

a.best: Absorb some heat leaving Earth and send some back

b.best: Planet X traps more heat and is warmer on average
